### I Cry to You and You Do Not Answer Me
Author: Jon Bloom
Site: Desiring God
URL: https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/i-cry-to-you-and-you-do-not-answer-me
Passage: Job 30:20-21
Points:
- Scripture is remarkably honest in recording the raw pain and doubts of faithful believers like Job.
- During prolonged suffering, God's silence can make Him feel distant, detached, or even cruel.
- God's seeming inaction never means He is absent; He is continually working out deeper purposes beyond our sight.
- Just as God redeemed Christ's suffering on the cross, He uses our inscrutable trials to prepare eternal glory.
- Believers facing unanswered prayers are encouraged to endure, trusting God’s promise to ultimately restore and strengthen them.
